raw_response:
I'm 48, been farming these 20 mu since I was 18 years old. Never went to school — can't read those technical pamphlets the extension people hand out. But I know cotton. I know every bump in these fields. It's just me and my husband at home now. Our children are working in the city and send a little money, but I don't like to ask them for farm money.

Twenty mu of cotton is a lot of work for two people, but we've managed it for years. I plant around April 20th, when the soil feels warm under your bare feet. I buy improved seed from the county supply shop — about 40 yuan per mu. I used to save my own seed, but the shop seed gives better bolls and fewer empty ones.

For fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — 50 jin bags, the ones with the three numbers on the bag. Old Chen at the shop told me once that it's about 6 kg of phosphorus and potassium, whatever those are. I just know my cotton looks greener and sets more bolls when I do it this way. Then when the flowers start showing in July, I topdress with urea — about 15 jin per mu. I tried skipping the topdress two years ago to save money, and the yield dropped badly. The bolls were small and light. Never again.

I irrigate twice. Once right after planting to get the seeds up, and once in late July when the bolls need water. Pumping from the well costs electricity, and I watch every yuan. My neighbor down the road irrigates three times, but his son has a factory job and helps with the bills. Two times is enough if the summer rain cooperates.

Pesticide — I can't skip it. Cotton bollworms will eat everything if you let them. I spray herbicide once after the cotton comes up to kill the weeds. Then insecticide four times through summer — early July, mid-July, early August, and late August if I still see worms. Me and my husband take turns with the backpack sprayer. Our shoulders ache for days after.

For tillage, I hire the village tractor in spring to plow and rotary till. Costs about 50 yuan per mu, but at our age we can't do it by hand anymore.

Picking is what keeps me up at night. Twenty mu means picking for over a month, going out every few days as the bolls open. Me and my husband do what we can, but we have to hire women from the village. We need about 30 days of hired labor for picking alone, at 150 yuan a day plus lunch. It's our biggest cost, but without it the cotton rots in the field.

I expect about 280 kg per mu if the weather is kind and the worms stay away. Last year I got about 260. I need a good year. My total costs will be about 10,500 yuan. That's a lot of cash to find at the start of the season, but I've learned the hard way that cutting corners costs more at harvest than it saves.
